Grenada Passport: Your Gateway to the US E-2 Visa

Grenada’s citizenship-by-investment program is unique among Caribbean programs. It gives qualifying investors a legal pathway to the US E-2 Investor Visa. Grenada has a bilateral investment treaty with the United States. This makes it the only Caribbean country with a CBI program that allows passport holders to apply for E-2 status.

Grenada established the program under its Citizenship by Investment Act 2013. The government regulates it, with two investment routes and defined eligibility criteria. Grenada has introduced a new physical-presence requirement into the legal framework, but it is not currently in effect. Its implementation has been deferred until the regional regulator is operational.

For qualifying investors seeking US market access alongside global mobility, Grenada is worth serious consideration.

How Does the Grenada E-2 Visa Work?

The E-2 treaty investor visa allows qualifying foreign nationals to enter and work in the United States. They must invest in a US-based enterprise. It is not a green card or a pathway to residency. But it provides a legal basis to live and run a business in the US.

Grenada CBI E-2 visa access works in two distinct stages.

Stage 1: Obtain Grenada Citizenship

You apply for and receive Grenada citizenship through the CBI program. This makes you a Grenadian national.

Stage 2: Apply for the US E-2 Visa

Grenada passport holders qualify for the E-2 treaty investor option. U.S. law requires an additional domicile for certain applicants. This applies to people who got treaty-country citizenship through financial investment.

If you don’t previously have E status, you’re required to get domicile before applying for an E-2 visa. The applicant must have been domiciled in Grenada for at least three consecutive years. This requirement is subject to U.S. law.

The current U.S. law allows E-2 visas issued to Grenadian nationals to be valid for five years, with multiple entries, subject to U.S. rules and eligibility. Your spouse and unmarried children under 21 may be eligible under the same visa.

How to Apply for Grenada Citizenship

Step 1: Choose your investment route

Qualifying investors have two options.

You can make a non-refundable donation to the National Transformation Fund (NTF). Or you can buy a share in a government-approved real estate development.

The minimum qualifying investment is US$235,000 for the NTF route for a single applicant or a family of up to 4, plus applicable government, due diligence, processing, and interview fees.

Real estate property remains subject to the program’s holding-period requirements and market conditions.

Step 2: Preliminary due diligence

The authorised agent conducts the background checks. This review identifies potential risks or eligibility issues. Your agent tells you whether you qualify based on the initial assessment.

Step 3: Document preparation

Your agent provides a document checklist. You submit your documents in an accurate manner. You must submit documents in English and appropriately legalised. This stage takes up to 30 days.

The applicant remains responsible for ensuring all information provided is accurate. You must complete all required forms and submit all documentation in the prescribed format.

Step 4: Submit the application

The authorized agent submits the application. The government authorities conduct their own due diligence and assess the application. The current process also requires the applicant to complete a mandatory interview.

Step 5: Make the investment

After receiving the required approval, the applicant must fulfil the selected investment requirement. At this stage, the authorized agent, like North Arista, will provide the applicant with the applicable timing requirements.

Step 6: Receive your passport

When your application is approved, Grenada issues the applicant’s Certificate of Naturalization. The applicant may then apply for a Grenadian passport and receive it through the prescribed channel.

Grenada Passport Visa-Free Countries

You can visit more than 140 destinations with a Grenadian passport. You don’t need a traditional visa in advance or on arrival. Your arrival is subject to each destination’s entry rules, permitted stay, and any other travel requirements.

Always verify current requirements before traveling.

Europe

Grenada citizenship offers visa-free short-stay access to the Schengen Area. You can visit France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, and the Netherlands for up to 90 days in any 180 days. Access is subject to each country’s applicable entry rules.

This access is for permitted short stays only. It does not grant the right to work.

United Kingdom (UK)

Grenada citizens can visit the UK for short stays without a traditional visa. But they must obtain the latest UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before travel, subject to UK immigration rules.

Asia

Grenada citizens can enter China, Singapore, and Hong Kong without a visa for short-stay visits. This depends on each country’s entry conditions and any applicable requirements.

United States

Grenadian passport holders can’t visit the US directly. But they may qualify for the E-2 investor visa. This is subject to U.S. immigration laws. Applicants who obtained Grenadian nationality through financial investment must be domiciled.

Holding a Grenadian passport does not guarantee E-2 approval. It establishes a legal route to apply.

Grenada Citizenship Requirements

The following eligibility criteria apply, subject to the program’s regulations.

Personal requirements

  • You must be at least 18 years old
  • You must meet Grenada’s character, security, and due diligence requirements.
  • You must be in good general health
  • Your investment funds must come from a legal and verifiable source

Investment requirements

Applicants broadly have two investment routes.

Option 1: NTF Donation

  • Single applicant: US$235,000
  • Applicant and spouse: US$235,000
  • Family (4 eligible members): US$235,000
  • Additional dependants: additional fees apply

Option 2: Real Estate

The minimum qualifying investment is US$270,000 in an approved project. There’s an additional US$50,000 government contribution. For projects outside the tourism sector, the minimum investment is US$350,000.

  • Alternative approved-project structures may require US$350,000
  • You can resell after the applicable five-year holding period
  • Additional government, processing, due diligence, and interview fees apply

Documents required

  • Valid passport from your country of origin
  • Certified birth certificate
  • Police clearance certificate
  • Medical examination and health certificate
  • Bank statements showing source of funds
  • Passport-size photographs
  • Marriage certificate (if applicable)
  • Proof of address

Submit all documents in English and legalise them before submission.

Grenada allows dual citizenship. You do not need to give up your nationality.

How Long Does Grenada Citizenship Take?

The application process typically takes three to four months. Additional time is required for investment fulfillment, naturalization and passport issuance.

Here is a general timeline:

  • Preliminary due diligence: Depends on the application
  • Document preparation: Up to 30 days
  • Government review and due diligence: 3 to 4 months
  • Investment fulfillment: Timing depends on the investment route

Government review takes time and depends on your personal and financial record. This may also require additional documentation.

Once your Grenada citizenship application is approved, you may begin the US E-2 visa process. You can handle this through a US Embassy or Consulate. The timeline depends on your application status.

Is Grenada a Good Second Passport?

The Grenada passport covers more than 140 destinations listed as visa-free, visa-on-arrival, or otherwise accessible without a traditional visa in advance. The US is not on Grenada’s visa-free list. But the E-2 treaty route offers an alternative for investors who want legitimate, renewable access to the US.

Grenada’s new physical-presence requirement has not yet taken effect. The implementation remains pending. Dual citizenship is permitted. You can include eligible dependants in the same application.

Who can you include as dependants?

Eligible dependants may include the following categories, subject to the program’s age, dependency, relationship, and other applicable requirements:

  • Your spouse
  • Dependent children who meet the program’s requirements
  • Certain dependent siblings who meet the program’s requirements
  • Certain dependent parents or grandparents who meet the program’s requirements

What to consider

The E-2 visa is separate from a Grenadian passport. This requires a qualifying investment in a US business enterprise. Grenada citizenship lets you apply for the visa, but it doesn’t guarantee approval. Approval is subject to U.S. laws.

Final Thoughts

Grenada’s citizenship-by-investment program is different. It is the only Caribbean CBI program whose citizens can apply for an E-2 investor visa. If your E-2 visa application is approved, you can visit the US and run a business.

Grenada passport offers broad international access, including Europe and the UK. You can keep your original citizenship. You can include eligible family members in the same application. You gain treaty-based eligibility to apply for a renewable US visa tied to a business investment.

Authorised agents manage the application, and a mandatory interview is part of the current process. The investment requirements are defined. The NTF limit is currently US$235,000 for a single applicant or family of up to four.

For qualifying investors who need both global mobility and a structured pathway into the US market, Grenada’s CBI program offers something real.
